headline: A 2020 law let veterans keep receiving VA education and work-study payments and extend GI Bill deadlines when schools closed during the COVID-19 emergency.
what_it_does: The law covers the period from March 1 to December 21, 2020. It lets the VA keep paying work-study and education allowances when a program is suspended by an emergency. If a veteran could not finish a course because a school or program closed temporarily, that payment will not count against their education benefit entitlement. It also extends time limits for using Montgomery GI Bill, Post-9/11 GI Bill, and vocational rehabilitation benefits when closures or executive orders prevent use.

who_it_affects.group: Student veterans using Montgomery GI Bill or Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits
who_it_affects.how: Their deadlines to use education benefits were extended, and payments for interrupted courses would not reduce their remaining entitlement.
The VA could keep paying work-study allowances during the emergency period.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans with service-connected disabilities in vocational rehabilitation training
who_it_affects.how: Time limits for vocational rehabilitation participation were extended when training was prevented by an emergency or executive order.

who_it_affects.group: Colleges and training programs that closed or suspended classes
who_it_affects.how: Veterans enrolled in their programs could receive continued VA payments and extended time to finish during closures.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted April 28, 2020, and applies to the covered period from March 1 to December 21, 2020.
